import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import pandas as pd

# Load the data from the csv file
cameras = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv', 
                      columns=['brand', 'model_year', 'megapixels', 'max_iso', 'weight_grams', 
                               'price_usd', 'sensor_type', 'has_video_4k', 'lens_mount', 'body_type'])

# Plot a histogram of megapixels distribution
sns.histplot(cameras['megapixels'], kde=True, bins=20)
plt.title('Distribution of Megapixels in Cameras')
plt.xlabel('Megapixels')
plt.ylabel('Frequency')
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Plot a bar chart of top 5 camera brands by average price
top_brands = cameras.groupby('brand')['price_usd'].mean().nlargest(5)
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.barplot(x=top_brands.index, y=top_brands.values)
plt.title('Top 5 Camera Brands by Average Price')
plt.xlabel('Brand')
plt.ylabel('Average Price (USD)')
plt.xticks(rotation=90)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output2.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Plot a scatter plot of price vs weight
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.scatterplot(x='weight_grams', y='price_usd', data=cameras)
plt.title('Price vs Weight of Cameras')
plt.xlabel('Weight (grams)')
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)')
plt.savefig('output3.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
